key_headlines.title: South Korea's May Exports Hit Record $87.8 Billion Driven by Semiconductor Boom
key_headlines.summary: South Korea's exports reached an all-time high of $87.8 billion in May with semiconductor exports surging 167.7% year-over-year, marking 12 consecutive months of export growth and maintaining a trade surplus of $27 billion.

key_headlines.title: KOSPI Surges 5% on US-Iran Peace Deal, Oil Prices Stabilize
key_headlines.summary: South Korean stock market jumped over 5% following the US-Iran ceasefire agreement, with oil prices falling to $80 per barrel and the won strengthening as geopolitical tensions eased.

key_headlines.title: Semiconductor Profits Soar 961% While K-Shaped Economic Divide Deepens
key_headlines.summary: The top 30 companies are projected to earn 175 trillion won in Q2 profits with semiconductors accounting for 84%, while non-semiconductor companies face declining earnings, intensifying Korea's polarization.

key_headlines.title: Seoul Apartment Jeonse Prices Jump 1.15% in May, Largest Rise Since 2015
key_headlines.summary: Seoul apartment leasehold prices surged 1.15% in May, the largest monthly increase in 11 years, while average apartment purchase prices exceeded 1 billion won for the first time.

key_headlines.title: Bank of Japan Expected to Raise Rates to 1% at Next Week's Policy Meeting
key_headlines.summary: The Bank of Japan is anticipated to raise its policy rate from 0.75% to 1.0% at its June 16 monetary policy meeting, following multiple rate hike signals.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy is experiencing a significant boost from the US-Iran ceasefire agreement, which has eased geopolitical tensions and stabilized global oil markets. The semiconductor sector continues to drive exports, with May exports reaching a record $87.8 billion and semiconductor shipments up 167.7% year-over-year. However, this growth is creating a stark K-shaped divide in the economy, with semiconductor companies thriving while non-semiconductor firms struggle with declining earnings. The stock market responded positively to the peace deal, with KOSPI jumping 5% and expectations for further gains approaching the 9,000-point level.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: South Korea's economic growth is expected to receive a slight boost from the US-Iran ceasefire, though inflation concerns persist despite lower oil prices. The Bank of Korea is monitoring inflationary pressures from exchange rates and import prices, with some analysts predicting rate increases as early as July. Global monetary policy faces a difficult balancing act as central banks navigate between supporting growth and controlling inflation triggered by the recent geopolitical crisis. Marginal firms continue to pose risks to the broader economy, with their persistence potentially constraining investment and employment growth in healthy companies.
sections.Financial Markets: Asian equity markets rallied strongly following the US-Iran peace deal, with Asian indices celebrating the reduction of geopolitical risk premiums. The KOSPI surged 5% early in trading, with 73% of listed stocks advancing simultaneously and expectations for further gains toward the 9,000-point level. Currency markets stabilized with the won appreciating toward 1,400 levels and oil futures falling to $80 per barrel, though upcoming Fed monetary policy decisions on June 17 represent a key variable. Foreign investors, however, continued their net selling position with $7.02 billion in outflows, while the bond market saw $560 million in inflows.
sections.Industry & Technology: South Korea's semiconductor industry continues to dominate export performance with sustained 167.7% year-over-year growth and three consecutive months exceeding $30 billion in monthly exports. Companies like Hanmi Global are expanding internationally with 62% of revenues from overseas operations in semiconductors, batteries, and infrastructure projects across the US, Middle East, and Europe. Global investment in clean energy reached a record $2.3 trillion in 2025, with electric vehicles capturing the largest share at $893 billion despite policy headwinds. Korean semiconductor equipment and parts suppliers showed strong performance alongside the market rally, positioning the sector for continued growth.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul's real estate market is experiencing multiple pressures with apartment jeonse (leasehold) prices jumping 1.15% in May, the largest monthly increase since April 2015, due to severe supply shortages. Average apartment purchase prices in Seoul surpassed 1 billion won for the first time, with prices rising simultaneously in sales, jeonse, and monthly rental markets. Regional markets are showing speculative buying patterns, with prices spreading from Dongtan and Suji to nearby Giheung as investors seek areas with favorable policies and semiconductor industry support. Price pressures are expected to continue absent effective policy interventions before the Chuseok holiday.
sections.International Economy: President Trump is escalating trade tensions by demanding France eliminate digital services taxes on US tech giants, threatening 100% tariffs on French wine exports worth approximately 15.8 trillion won if the demand is not met. The US-Iran ceasefire agreement is reducing global geopolitical risk premiums and stabilizing energy markets, though central banks face continued inflation pressures. The Strait of Hormuz, which handles approximately 20% of global crude oil shipments, is expected to reopen under the peace agreement, though debates continue over potential transit tolls. The Federal Reserve's June 16-17 FOMC meeting remains a critical variable for global financial markets and currency movements.
sections.AI & Economy: South Korea and Japan are strengthening industrial cooperation in artificial intelligence, focusing on power efficiency for AI systems and care robots to address aging societies and labor shortages. China's large language models are rapidly gaining market share through cost-effectiveness, with DeepSeek's token usage ranking first weekly as AI agents increasingly prioritize cost efficiency over performance. The South Korean government is launching projects to develop domestic AI semiconductors with Samsung's participation, recognizing the importance of non-memory semiconductor competitiveness. Chinese AI models are expected to capture routine tasks while American models dominate complex work, creating a bifurcated market structure.
sections.Others: The Power Exchange has completed redundancy in its power control and market operations by opening a central headquarters in Osong, Chungbuk, ensuring uninterrupted grid operations during disasters. Investment in space infrastructure is accelerating following SpaceX's anticipated listing, with Kiwoom Asset Management launching an exchange-traded fund with up to 25% SpaceX exposure. AI adoption is rapidly displacing workers across Chinese manufacturing facilities, raising concerns about labor displacement despite economic growth potential. Political tensions have emerged in the US with controversial comments at a UFC event held at the White House, reflecting broader social divisions.
